bib.title: Advancing LLM Reasoning Generalists with Preference Trees

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only (lineage); all body, tables and appendices A-E read.

question: How can high-quality tree-structured alignment data and a study of preference learning algorithms improve open LLMs' reasoning across math, code and logic?
hypothesis: Reasoning performance after preference learning correlates with the absolute reward of chosen data; DPO, which optimises only relative reward margins, is less suited to reasoning than KTO and NCA.
contributions: ULTRAINTERACT, a multi-turn reasoning alignment dataset with preference trees (86K instructions, 220K action pairs)
EURUS-7B and EURUS-70B LLMs with state-of-the-art open-source results on reasoning benchmarks
Analysis of preference learning for reasoning (DPO vs KTO vs NCA), leading to a new reward-modeling objective and EURUS-RM-7B

method.summary: ULTRAINTERACT collects, for each hard reasoning instruction, a binary preference tree of correct/incorrect actions from actor models interacting with a Python interpreter and a GPT-4 critique. EURUS-7B/70B are SFT'd from Mistral-7B/CodeLLaMA-70B on correct actions plus general chat data, then preference-tuned with DPO, KTO or NCA. EURUS-RM-7B adds a reward term LDR to the Bradley-Terry loss to push chosen rewards up and rejected rewards down.
method.task: reasoning alignment: SFT, preference optimisation and reward modeling for math, coding and logic

datasets.name: ULTRAINTERACT
datasets.split: SFT uses all correct actions (287K), preference learning uses 220K multi-turn pairs, RM uses 220K plus 240K single-turn augmented pairs
datasets.source: 12 datasets: GSM8K, MATH, MathQA, NumGLUE, TabMWP, CodeContest, TACO, WikiTableQuestions, Magicoder-Evol-Instruct, ReClor, HotpotQA, StrategyQA; problems GPT-3.5-Turbo fails; trees capped at 5 turns
datasets.preprocessing: 8-gram exact-match decontamination against test sets of the same task; Exact Substring Matching for LeetCode; instances failing Python syntax check excluded

datasets.name: UltraChat / ShareGPT / OpenOrca
datasets.size: 7B SFT mix: 32K UltraChat, 30K ShareGPT, 50K OpenOrca; 70B mix: 63K UltraChat, 30K ShareGPT, 70K OpenOrca
datasets.source: Ding et al. 2023; openchat sharegpt4; Lian et al. 2023

datasets.name: UltraFeedback
datasets.split: all pairs, used in preference learning and reward modeling

datasets.name: HumanEval, MBPP, LeetCode, GSM-Plus, MATH, TheoremQA, SVAMP, ASDiv, BBH, IFEval, MINT, MMLU, MT-Bench
datasets.source: cited benchmarks; all but MATH are OOD

datasets.name: RewardBench (no prior sets), AutoJ, MT-Bench
datasets.source: Lambert et al. 2024; Li et al. 2023a; Zheng et al. 2023

other.note: DPO on 70B fails, rewards go to -inf; no 70B DPO row

other.use: actor model for correct actions; also GPT-4 Turbo escalated for hard problems
one randomly sampled to produce each incorrect action; also Table 2 baselines

training.objective: SFT on correct leaf actions; DPO / KTO / NCA for preference learning; RM loss L = L_BT + L_DR, L_BT = -log sigma(r(x,yc)-r(x,yr)), L_DR = -log sigma(r(x,yc)) - log sigma(-r(x,yr)), with L_DR applied only to ULTRAINTERACT instances (others use L_BT)
training.epochs: 1 epoch for SFT, preference learning and RM

other.sft_note: interaction history discarded; train only on correct leaf nodes of each tree
other.rm_pair_augmentation: match each correct action with one incorrect action of other turns (NxN pairs for depth N); drop same-turn pairs; keep instructions with NxN <= 10; sample at most 9 pairs with each action used no more than 3 times; yields 240k single-turn pairs

inference.samples: reranking: N = 2, 4, 8, 16 responses per instruction from Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2; other eval samples not stated
inference.prompting: 0-shot CoT except BBH (3-shot) and IFEval (no CoT); 5-shot MMLU; math: both textual and program-enhanced settings, best of the two reported

other.data_construction_sampling: sample 20 actions and keep a random correct one; repeat up to 3 times escalating to GPT-4 Turbo; else give ground-truth rationales and answers

GPT-3.5/GPT-4 numbers from previous works. Most RM baseline results copied from Jiang et al. 2023b and Lambert et al. 2024.

limits: Explanation that DPO fails because chosen reward falls is a correlational hypothesis from three algorithms and one model family; no controlled intervention besides the RM ablation.
DPO 70B run failed so the comparison exists only at 7B.
No seeds, variance, optimizer, batch size, sequence length, precision or hardware are stated; decoding settings are not given.
TheoremQA numbers for MAmmoTH, OpenChat and Starling-LM are contaminated and struck through.
Data relies on GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4 and GPT-4 Turbo as actor and critique; Magicoder subset excluded from preference pairs because correctness is judged by GPT-4 Turbo.
Training only on ULTRAINTERACT harms instruction following (IFEval 17.4), so it must be mixed with general data.
Datasets are restricted to problems with ground truth, so the recipe does not cover open-ended tasks.

terms.definition: A tree per instruction with the instruction as root and each action a node; a trajectory is a root-to-leaf path; correct nodes serve SFT and paired correct/incorrect nodes serve preference learning.
Additional reward-model term -log sigma(r(x,yc)) - log sigma(-r(x,yr)) that increases the reward of chosen and decreases that of rejected actions.
